newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Alliance & Leicester ups profits.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Alliance & Leicester ups profits.

text.p: UK building society Alliance & Leicester said on Tuesday it was very pleased with its results for the first half of the year, which showed it is on a sound footing for its conversion to bank status next year.
"We regard them as a very solid set of results," group finance director Richard Pym told Reuters in an interview.
Earlier the building society announced pre-tax profits for the six months to June 30 of 183 million stg, a 12 percent rise on the same period in 1995 when it made 163 million stg.
Pym said the results higlighted the society's strong financial foundations and its conservative lending policies.
The society's timetable for a stock market flotation next year was "spot on" and its members would be able to vote on the conversion to bank status later this year, Pym said.

Pym said the cost of conversion would be around 15 stg a head for each of the society's 3.5 million members, with much of this covering postage costs and other overheads associated with share applications.

He declined to say whether there would be a special general meeting for shareholders to vote on the conversion, but said the building society would be announcing the scheme under which this will take place later this year.
Pym said he could not say how many of the society's customers would withdraw savings once the conversion had taken place and they had received any shares due to them.

"We have had good retail funding in the first half of this year," he said, adding the society had stemmed inflows early on and it had not been overwhelmed with investors to the same extent as other societies which were tipped to convert and make a one-off pay-out to their savers and borrowers.
He said one of the main reasons for conversion to bank status was that Alliance & Leicester would be better placed to make acquisitions, but did not detail what these might be.
"Most of the foundations have now been laid down for a successful diversified financial services group," Pym said, adding there were no new acquisitions in the pipeline.

But future expansion would include greater commercial lending via Girobank, its money transmission subsidiary, and the provision of merchant acquisition, the processing of electronic debit and credit card payments.
The relationship with Post Office Counters Ltd, which provides a network of nearly 20,000 post office outlets for Girobank customers, remains excellent, he added.
Pym said the society was looking at the electronic possibilities of home banking but would stick to telephone banking as its main focus for the immediate future.

He said there had been a recent "gentle upward movement" in Alliance & Leicester's mortgage lending business with the ending of "some of the more ludicrous deals" offered my some other mortgage lenders earlier this year.
But the mortgage market was still very favourable to consumers, he added. A gradual increase in house prices should remove negative equity and increase the number of housing transactions.
"A gentle move upward in housing prices is what we are expecting," Pym said.
